title: Anemic Domain Model with DTO Duplication
pattern: An application model where domain entities are dumb data containers (getter/setter bags) paired with identical Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) and assembler classes used strictly inside the same process space.
why_bad:
*   **Accidental Complexity:** Duplicating the data schema across identical structs requires maintenance in multiple places and forces unnecessary in-memory object copying and allocations.
*   **Procedural Logic:** Business rules leak into external "Services" or "Assemblers" instead of being safely encapsulated behind entity boundaries.
detection: Struct pairs in the same crate with $\ge 90\%$ field similarity and matching names (one ending in `Dto`), coordinated by stateless "Assembler" or "Converter" routines.
counterexample: **Strict Serialization Boundary:** DTOs are valid when they represent a stable, versioned public API wire format that must not change when internal domain structures are refactored.
source: Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 14 "Application" & Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture*, Chapter 15 "Data Transfer Object".
